title: Generator-normalized unit and Tate-line endpoints for derived scalar extension
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $N\in\mathbf N$, and $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital homomorphism of commutative rings with $NA=NB=0$. Use the constant module sheaves and finite Tate lines $R_T$ and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}R_T$, with their power action, of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class], and the ordinary etale derived extension $E_\varphi:D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], adjoint to exact restriction. Define a normalized endpoint datum to consist of maps $\eta^0:A_T\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi B_T$ and $\eta^1:A_T(1)\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi B_T(1)$, sending local constant generators $a$ to $\varphi(a)$ and root tensors $z\otimes a$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)$, together with isomorphisms $d^0:E_\varphi(A_T)\simeq B_T$ and $d^1:E_\varphi(A_T(1))\simeq B_T(1)$. Their homs must be exactly the derived-adjunction transposes of $\eta^0[0]$ and $\eta^1[0]$, using the canonical exact restriction/single comparison. The shifted line comparison is the canonical adjoint shift comparison followed by $d^1[2]$. For a fixed arrow $c:A_T\to A_T(1)[2]$, define its scalar image to be $(d^0)^{-1}$ followed by $E_\varphi(c)$ and that shifted line comparison. The residue coefficient ring is $\mathbf Z/N$, lifted to the sheaf coefficient universe, and its map to a ring killed by $N$ is the unique unital residue map. These are definitions only; existence of endpoint data is not asserted.
